blocks.text: 1. CBOW

blocks.alt: Context words go through CBOW to predict the target word

blocks.text: Word2Vec, the previous topic, introduced two variants for learning word embeddings. CBOW is a complete, dedicated look at Word2Vec's first variant, explored throughout this topic.
Continuous Bag of Words works by predicting a target word from its genuinely surrounding context, a genuinely specific prediction direction covered throughout the rest of this topic.

3. The Prediction Direction

blocks.alt: Context words predict the target word

blocks.text: CBOW's genuinely defining direction connects back to the context window, already covered in Word2Vec. Given the genuinely surrounding context words, genuinely predict the single target word in the middle.
This is a genuinely specific, direct application of the core idea already covered generally in Word2Vec, choosing genuinely context-to-word as its own particular direction.

blocks.text: 4. What "Bag Of Words" Genuinely Means

blocks.alt: Context words have their order not considered

blocks.text: This connects back to position-wise independence, already covered in Feed-Forward Networks. The genuinely "bag" in CBOW's own name means word order within the context genuinely gets ignored.
The genuinely context words simply get averaged together, without regard to their own specific position, giving this technique its own genuinely descriptive, distinctive name.
5. Averaging Context Vectors

blocks.alt: Word 1 and word 2 vectors average into a combined context vector

blocks.text: This connects back to the weighted sum, already covered in the Convolution Operation. CBOW genuinely averages the embedding vectors of every context word together, a genuinely simple, direct combination.

This produces a genuinely single, combined representation used to predict the target word, directly reusing the summation idea already covered in that earlier topic in a genuinely new, specific context.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This averaging step, already covered in this topic, is exactly what the "bag of words" name already covered in this topic refers to: individual word identities and positions genuinely blend together into one combined signal.

blocks.text: 6. Why CBOW Is Genuinely Less Computationally Intensive

blocks.alt: CBOW makes one prediction while Skip-gram makes multiple predictions

blocks.text: A genuinely real, practical efficiency benefit connects back to a genuinely shallow architecture, already covered in Word2Vec. Averaging genuinely multiple context words into one input genuinely means fewer training predictions per sentence.

This is a genuinely real, practical efficiency benefit compared to the alternative direction explored in the very next topic of this module, directly extending the efficiency already covered generally in Word2Vec.
7. CBOW Genuinely Suits Frequent Words

blocks.alt: CBOW works well for frequent words

blocks.text: This connects back to the training objective, already covered generally throughout this course. CBOW's own averaging tends to genuinely smooth out rare, unusual context words, already covered as a genuine consequence of that averaging step.

This makes it genuinely especially effective for learning representations of genuinely frequent, common words, a genuinely real, practical strength directly resulting from the averaging already covered earlier in this topic.
8. A Concrete Architectural Summary
A genuinely concrete architectural summary connects back to multiple context words genuinely feeding in, each looked up in the embedding table, already covered in Embeddings.

These get averaged together, then genuinely used to predict the single target word through the hidden layer, already covered in Word2Vec, completing the genuinely full, concrete CBOW pipeline covered throughout this topic.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When CBOW Is Genuinely The Right Variant

blocks.alt: Needing faster training on frequent words points toward CBOW

blocks.text: This connects back to genuinely large training corpora with genuinely common, frequent words, already covered in this topic. CBOW, already covered in this topic, trains genuinely faster and works genuinely well here.

This connects back to Skip-gram, covered in the very next topic, favoring genuinely rare words instead. CBOW, already covered, remains the genuinely more efficient choice when that specific need does not apply.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates CBOW's own context-averaging computation, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
embedding_dimension = 4
vocabulary = {"the": 0, "quick": 1, "brown": 2, "fox": 3, "jumps": 4}

embedding_table = rng.normal(size=(len(vocabulary), embedding_dimension)) * 0.1  # already covered as Embeddings

sentence = ["the", "quick", "brown", "fox", "jumps"]
target_index = 2  # "brown" is the target, already covered as the prediction direction in this topic
context_words = [sentence[1], sentence[3]]  # "quick" and "fox", already covered as the context window

context_vectors = np.array([embedding_table[vocabulary[word]] for word in context_words])
averaged_context = context_vectors.mean(axis=0)  # already covered as averaging context vectors in this topic

print(f"Target word: '{sentence[target_index]}'")
print(f"Context words (already covered as bag of words, order-independent): {context_words}")
print(f"Averaged context vector: {np.round(averaged_context, 3)}")
print("\nThis averaged vector, already covered in this topic, would then genuinely predict the target word through the hidden layer already covered in Word2Vec")

blocks.content: Running this example shows the two context word embeddings genuinely averaged into a single combined vector, exactly the process already covered throughout this topic as CBOW's own core mechanism.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: CBOW, Continuous Bag of Words, predicts a target word from its surrounding context.
It is the first of Word2Vec's two variants.
The "bag" in its name means word order within the context gets ignored.
Context word embeddings get averaged together into a single combined representation.
This averaging means fewer training predictions per sentence, a real efficiency benefit.
Averaging tends to smooth out rare words, making CBOW especially effective for frequent, common words.
The full pipeline: context words looked up, averaged, then used to predict the target word.
It suits large corpora with common, frequent words well.
Next up: Skip-gram, Word2Vec's other variant, predicting context from a single word instead.
